sourcePacket.title: Python Language Reference: Boolean operations
claims: Short-circuit evaluation for Python's and operator evaluates the left operand first; if it is false, that operand is returned without evaluating the right operand, otherwise the right operand is evaluated and returned.

captures.locator: Boolean operations, paragraph describing x and y
captures.capturedText: The expression x and y first evaluates x; if x is false, its value is returned; otherwise, y is evaluated.

term.df: For Python's and operator, a false left operand is returned and the right operand is skipped instead of being evaluated.
term.eg: With a false left operand, Python returns that operand without evaluating the right operand.
term.mi: Python and always evaluates both operands before choosing a Boolean result.
term.cx: The right operand is skipped when the left operand is false, rather than both operands always being evaluated.

sourcePacket.title: Python Glossary: hashable
claims: Python lists and dictionaries are not hashable, while tuples and frozensets are hashable only when all of their elements are hashable.

captures.capturedText: An object is hashable if it has a hash value which never changes during its lifetime (it needs a __hash__() method), and can be compared to other objects (it needs an __eq__() method).
Mutable containers such as lists or dictionaries are not hashable; tuples and frozensets are only hashable if their elements are hashable.

term.df: A Python tuple is hashable only when every element stored inside that tuple is itself hashable.
term.eg: A tuple containing a list is not hashable because its list element is not hashable.
term.mi: Every tuple is hashable simply because the outer tuple container is immutable.
term.cx: A tuple is hashable only when all its elements are hashable, not merely because the outer container is immutable.

sourcePacket.title: The Science of Earthquakes
claims: The P-wave and S-wave arrival interval records the faster P wave first, and the time between P and S arrivals becomes larger as a station is farther from the earthquake.

captures.locator: How can scientists tell where the earthquake happened?, wave-speed paragraph
captures.capturedText: P waves are also faster than S waves, and this fact is what allows us to tell where an earthquake was.

captures.locator: How can scientists tell where the earthquake happened?, arrival-gap paragraph
captures.capturedText: If you are close to the earthquake, the P and S wave will come one right after the other, but if you are far away, there will be more time between the two.

term.df: The arrival interval is the time between the faster P wave arriving first and the S wave following later.
term.eg: A station farther from the earthquake records a larger delay between its P-wave and S-wave arrivals.
term.mi: The P-wave and S-wave arrival interval becomes smaller as a station gets farther from the earthquake.
term.cx: The arrival interval grows with station distance, rather than shrinking as the station moves farther away.

sourcePacket.title: What are igneous rocks?
claims: Igneous cooling rate and crystal texture are linked: intrusive magma cools slowly underground and develops relatively large grains, whereas extrusive lava cools quickly near the surface and develops fine-grained or glassy texture.

captures.capturedText: Slow cooling means the individual mineral grains have a very long time to grow, so they grow to a relatively large size.
Quick cooling means that mineral crystals don't have much time to grow, so these rocks have a very fine-grained or even glassy texture.

term.tr: Igneous cooling rate and crystal texture
term.df: Cooling rate controls the time available for mineral growth, linking slow cooling to coarse grains and rapid cooling to fine texture.
term.eg: Slow cooling gives mineral grains a long time to grow; quick cooling produces fine-grained or glassy texture.
term.mi: Rapid cooling gives mineral crystals more time to grow and therefore creates a coarse-grained rock.
term.cx: Slow cooling permits larger crystals, whereas rapid cooling limits growth instead of producing coarse grains.

sourcePacket.title: Scales and scale degrees
claims: A major scale uses the ordered step pattern whole, whole, half, whole, whole, whole, half from tonic to the octave.

captures.capturedText: A major scale consists of seven whole and half steps in the following succession: W-W-H-W-W-W-H.

term.df: A major scale orders its seven adjacent steps as whole, whole, half, whole, whole, whole, then half.
term.eg: A learner checks seven successive scale steps against the W-W-H-W-W-W-H major-scale pattern.
term.mi: A major scale alternates whole steps and half steps evenly from tonic to octave.
term.cx: The pattern is W-W-H-W-W-W-H, not an even alternation of whole and half steps.

sourcePacket.title: La in the Bass at Beginnings, Middles, and Endings
claims: Deceptive motion most commonly occurs when dominant V moves to vi rather than I.

captures.capturedText: Deceptive motion most commonly occurs when V moves to vi rather than I, with the bass moving sol-la.

term.df: Deceptive motion most commonly moves dominant V to vi rather than moving that dominant to I.
term.eg: A dominant V moving to vi rather than I demonstrates the most common deceptive motion.
term.mi: The common deceptive pattern reverses the order, moving vi to V rather than moving V to vi.
term.cx: V is the starting harmony and vi is the destination; the common motion is V-to-vi, not vi-to-V.
